passage:
Subject: Confession, and a small plan

Pooja,

Kabir got picked to lead the client demo on Thursday. He has been here eight months. I've been here three years, and I felt the sting straight away, a hot little thing in my chest, and then I was short with him in stand-up. 😅 Not proud of that. I stayed up half the night sulking, then got bored of sulking and admitted it: he's faster than me with the data. So today I asked Kabir to walk me through his model, and I told our manager the layout idea for the demo was his. I also signed up for the modelling course I kept postponing. It still stings a little. Tell me if I'm overdoing the noble bit.

Irfan

qa.q: How long has Kabir been at the company?
qa.a: Kabir has been there eight months.

qa.q: Why was Irfan short with Kabir in stand-up?
qa.a: Irfan felt a sting of envy in the chest after Kabir was picked to lead the demo, and it came out as sharpness.

qa.q: What steps did Irfan take after admitting the envy?
qa.a: Irfan asked Kabir to explain the model, credited Kabir to the manager for the layout idea, and signed up for the course Irfan had been postponing.

qa.q: How might Kabir have felt about Irfan's short manner in stand-up?
qa.a: Kabir may have been confused or uneasy, not knowing the reason, and may have felt more welcome once Irfan asked to learn from the model.

grounding: A talented junior progresses faster; Irfan notices the envy, then shares credit, learns from the junior and keeps building own skills.

passage:
I'm Hrithik. Two years ago, a junior named Jasleen joined my team at the Gurgaon consulting firm. Within six months, she was presenting to clients I'd spent three years winning over. The partners loved her.

I noticed the sting at a team dinner, when the senior partner said, "Jasleen's going places." I smiled and felt sick.

For a few weeks, I did small, ugly things. I didn't forward her an email about a big project. I let her struggle with a spreadsheet I could have fixed in five minutes.

Then I caught myself. That wasn't who I wanted to be. And honestly, it was hurting the team.

So I did the opposite. I recommended her for the project. I credited her work by name in a partner meeting. And I signed up for a course on the financial modelling I'd been avoiding.

We work well together now. And I've grown too. Her speed pushed me.

qa.q: How long did it take Jasleen to present to clients Hrithik had spent years winning?
What did Hrithik feel when the senior partner praised Jasleen?
qa.a: Hrithik felt a sting of envy, smiling while feeling sick inside.

qa.q: What did Hrithik change once he noticed his envy?
qa.a: Hrithik stopped holding Jasleen back, recommended her for the project, credited her by name, and worked on Hrithik's own skills.

qa.q: How might Jasleen have been affected by Hrithik's early behaviour?
qa.a: Jasleen may have felt frustrated and unsupported, missing an important email and struggling alone with the spreadsheet.

grounding: The reflective account shows someone threatened by a talented junior's progress, noticing the envy, and choosing to share opportunities, give credit and keep growing.

passage:
Studio manager's note, animation team, Friday

I've been watching Reena, one of our lead animators, over the past month. Thomas, the junior she's been training since January, has become remarkably fast. The client asked for him by name on Monday.

I noticed Reena's face tighten in that meeting. Later I saw her assign Thomas only the dull background work for two weeks.

Today she came to my office herself. She said, "I've been keeping Thomas away from the good shots. I think I'm jealous. He's better than I was at his age, and it scares me."

I thanked her for being honest. I said envy is human, but holding him back hurts the whole team, and her too.

She decided to hand Thomas the lead on the next client scene and to credit him in the review. She also asked to join the new 3D workshop for herself.

Next step: I'll check in with both of them after the client review.

Studio manager

qa.q: Who did the client ask for by name?
What was Reena feeling when she came to the manager's office?
qa.a: She felt envious and scared, admitting Thomas was better than she had been at his age.

qa.q: What did Reena decide to do, and why is it wise?
qa.a: Give Thomas the lead on the next scene, credit him in the review and take a 3D workshop, which supports the team and keeps her growing.

qa.q: How might Thomas have felt during the two weeks of background work?
qa.a: He may have felt confused or sidelined, not knowing why he was kept from the good shots.

grounding: A manager's note shows a senior noticing envy of a talented junior, admitting it, and choosing to share opportunities, give credit and keep growing her own skills.
